scope: Public-source historical metadata framework extending the repository timeline back to the 1500s and forward through 2027.
coverage_statement: For the 1500s through the early modern period, metadata means surviving archival/catalog information about manuscripts, maps, laws, administrative records, financial records, correspondence, printed books, artifacts, and archaeological records. There is no complete metadata corpus for this period, and many records were never created, did not survive, remain uncatalogued, or are held in collections not digitized online.

periods.status: future year; no future records represented

provenance_rules: Distinguish original record from later transcription, translation, catalog description, or digitization
Record uncertainty in dates and authorship
Do not infer missing historical events from absence of surviving records
Treat later historical interpretations separately from primary-source metadata
Record repository and collection context when available
Preserve alternate spellings/names as historical metadata without treating them as separate entities unless justified
privacy_and_security_boundary: no classified material obtained through unauthorized means
no re-identification of living private persons
no destructive probing of archives or services
research_limitations: Digitization is highly uneven before the 20th century
Catalog records can be incomplete or revised
Historical records may use obsolete calendars, place names, languages, and naming conventions
Metadata may describe an item without exposing the full item
Some archival collections have access restrictions based on preservation, ownership, law, or donor terms
A single global metadata scan is not technically or historically possible
status: Historical metadata framework added to Prev_NW; it extends the repository's structured timeline to the 1500s without claiming nonexistent or inaccessible records.
